previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, and prior venous thrombosis was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, distention, and vomiting. Imaging showed bowel distention consistent with paralytic ileus rather than mechanical obstruction, with a known colonic stricture unchanged from prior studies. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, an NG tube, IV fluids, and IV hydromorphone for pain. Ciprofloxacin and metronidazole were continued for a presumed Crohn’s flare, and fondaparinux was maintained for prior upper extremity DVT. Her pain was partially complicated by PTSD, which was managed with diazepam and supportive care. The NG tube was removed after she tolerated oral intake, and pain control was transitioned to oral hydromorphone. She improved over nine days, was discharged home on oral medications, and scheduled for outpatient GI follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o female with a PMH of Crohn's disease s/p multiple 
resections and repeated episodes of obstruction who presented to 
the ED with 1 day of progressively worsening lower abdominal 
pain, abdominal distention, and 1 day of NBNB vomiting 
transferred from MICU to ___ 2 on HD 2 in stable condition with 
multiple days of nausea bloating and pain despite NGT/NPO in the 
setting of an abscence of objective obstructive findings.

A detailed problem list is as follows:
.
# Abdominal pain, fever, chills: Pain was in the setting of 
known Crohn's and s/p multiple resections with a history of 
recurrent partial obstructions; presentation was similar to 
previous episodes with the exception of new chills, fever to 101 
and gap acidosis - the latter resolved the second day of 
admission. Started on Cipro/Flagyl for a presumed Crohn's flare 
with possible bacterial translocation into the abdomen and 
subsequently defervesced. Underwent colonoscopy and balloon 
dilation as detailed above. Subsequent to colonscopy and the 
initiation of antibiotics, symptoms gradually improved with 
bowel rest and intermittent NGT suction. Rifaxamin was started 
per GI for bacterial overgrowth. Pain was managed with IV 
dilaudid titrated to effect in conjunction with valium in the 
acute setting; as her clinical status stabilized, these 
medications were downtitrated and transitioned to PO as 
permitted by negotiations with the patient. Diet was advanced as 
tolerated. Discharged in stable condition with no significant 
abdominal pain, no nausea, and tolerating a full diet. In 
addition to the diazepam detailed below, was also discharged 
with a 14 day prescription of PO dilaudid with an oral agreement 
made to follow-up with Dr. ___ days after discharge to 
assess her pain regimen.
.  
# Crohn's Disease: Presumed to be the primary etiology of the 
patient's presentation. Dr. ___ team consulted and 
recommended continuing Cipro/Flagyl until the patient was 
asymptomatic in addition to the diet and pain management as 
detailed above; she was also treated with a course of Rifaximin 
for bacterial overgrowth and was discharged on this medication. 
The patient was discharged with close follow-up with Dr. ___ 
and with her PCP.
.
# PTSD/Depression/Anxiety: Continued home citalopram. IV 
diazepam weaned over the course of the hospitalization and 
discharged with 14 days of diazepam with an oral agreement that 
she was to self-downtitrate and follow-up with her PCP regarding 
whether to continue this medication in 2 weeks.
.
# Iron deficiency anemia: Treated with IV iron dextran and 
ferric gluconate as an inpatient.
.
# Acute renal insufficiency: Creatinine normalized from 1.1 on 
admission to baseline 0.6 with PO hydration.
.  
# RUE extremity swelling: Pt w/ Chronic narrowing of the SVC, 
including a focal segment of wall thickening/chronic thrombus 
along its anterior margin. DVT was ruled out with RU dopplers 
and swelling resolved after one day with warm compresses and 
elevation.

# Hypothyroidism: Clinically euthyroid during the 
hospitalization on home synthroid.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with Crohn's disease, status post multiple

performed after administration of oral contrast.  Axial, coronal and sagittal
reformats were acquired.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS:

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:  

There is minimal basilar atelectasis at the right lung.  

Assessment of solid visceral structures is limited without intravenous
contrast.  Allowing for this, the liver is normal.  There is no intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  The pancreas, spleen, both adrenal glands
and kidneys are normal. Gallbladder is nonvisualized.

There are multiple scattered non-pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal lymph
nodes.  Redemonstrated are multiple mesenteric lymph nodes, predominantly at
the right lower quadrant measuring up to 9 mm, unchanged.
There are no significant atherosclerotic calcifications of the abdominal
arterial system.

There is no free air and no free fluid.

The small bowel is filled with contrast without evidence of bowel wall
thickening or small bowel obstruction.  The patient had multiple prior both
small and large bowel resections with a neoterminal ileum in the right mid
abdomen.  There is unchanged mild dilatation of the neoterminal ileum proximal
to the anastomosis site (series 2, image 41) and mild large bowel wall
thickening and narrowing distal to the anastomosis site (series 2, image 43),
unchanged from prior exam and likely representing a fixed stenosis and chronic
postinflammatory change.

CT OF THE PELVIS: 

The large bowel is air filled and slightly dilated.  There are multiple new
areas of bowel wall thickening and narrowing in between areas of mildly
dilated large bowel loops, predominantly at the sigmoid colon (series 2, image
64, series 2, image 70 and series 2, image 70). However, this most likely
represents bowel peristalis as these were not present in the study of
___, and are thus less likely skip lesions from Crohn disease.

There is no free fluid in the pelvis.  The urinary bladder, vagina are normal.
There are no pelvic hernias.

BONES:  

There are bilateral chronic sacroiliitis.  No evidence of suspicious lytic or
sclerotic bony lesions.  There are calcified granulomas in the soft tissues
overlying large gluteal muscles likely from prior subcutaneous injections.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of small or large bowel obstruction.

2.  Multiple areas of large bowel wall pseudo-thickening and narrowing, new
compared to prior, likely represents peristalsis, less likely consistent skip
lesions; however, evaluation is limited without oral and IV contrast.

3.  Unchanged fixed narrowing of large bowel distal to the anastomosis site
with the neoterminal ileum with mild dilatation of the neoterminal ileum.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Written informed consent was obtained prior to the
procedure with the indication, alternatives, risks and benefits explained. 
The patient demonstrated good understanding of these features.  The patient
was brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.
The right side of the neck was prepped and draped in the typical sterile

medical record number as identifiers.

Under sonographic guidance, the right internal jugular vein was accessed with
a micropuncture set and images were saved to PACS.  A 0.035 ___ wire was
placed through the micropuncture sheath and advanced into the inferior vena
cava under fluoroscopic guidance after taking appropriate measurements. 
Micropuncture sheath was removed and the soft tissue tract was dilated.  A 7
___, 16 cm temporary triple-lumen central venous catheter was placed over
the Guidewire and the Guidewire was removed.  All three ports of the catheter
were aspirated and flushed easily.  Catheter was secured to the skin with 0
silk sutures and a sterile dressing was applied.  A fluoroscopic chest film
was obtained demonstrating satisfactory placement of the catheter with the tip
terminating in the distal SVC.  The patient tolerated the procedure well and
there were no immediate complications.

jugular central venous catheter with the tip terminating in the distal SVC.
The line is ready for use.
